claim: Proteasomes are essential molecular machines responsible for the degradation of proteins in eukaryotic cells.
source: Proteasomes are essential molecular machines responsible for the degradation of proteins in eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about proteasomes.

claim: Altered proteasome activity has been linked to neurodegeneration, auto-immune disorders and cancer.
source: Altered proteasome activity has been linked to neurodegeneration, auto-immune disorders and cancer.
evidence: This statement references established connections in the literature between proteasome dysfunction and disease.

claim: No method currently exists to monitor proteasome composition and interactions in vivo in animal models.
source: Despite the relevance for human disease and drug development, no method currently exists to monitor proteasome composition and interactions in vivo in animal models.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work.

claim: A new mouse model was generated enabling the quantification of proteasome interactions by mass spectrometry.
source: To fill this gap, we developed a strategy based on tagging of proteasomes with promiscuous biotin ligases and generated a new mouse model enabling the quantification of proteasome interactions by mass spectrometry.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study describing the generation of a mouse model.

claim: Biotin ligases can be incorporated in fully assembled proteasomes without negative impact on their activity.
source: We show that biotin ligases can be incorporated in fully assembled proteasomes without negative impact on their activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: ProteasomeID enables the identification of novel proteasome-interacting proteins.
source: We demonstrate the utility of our method by identifying novel proteasome-interacting proteins, charting interactomes across mouse organs, and showing that proximity-labeling enables the identification of both endogenous and small-molecule-induced proteasome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: ProteasomeID enables charting of proteasome interactomes across mouse organs.
source: We demonstrate the utility of our method by identifying novel proteasome-interacting proteins, charting interactomes across mouse organs, and showing that proximity-labeling enables the identification of both endogenous and small-molecule-induced proteasome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data from multiple mouse organs.

claim: Proximity-labeling enables the identification of both endogenous and small-molecule-induced proteasome substrates.
source: We demonstrate the utility of our method by identifying novel proteasome-interacting proteins, charting interactomes across mouse organs, and showing that proximity-labeling enables the identification of both endogenous and small-molecule-induced proteasome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data using proteasome inhibitors and PROTACs.

claim: The ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS) is a major selective protein degradation system of eukaryotic cells.
source: The ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS) is a major selective protein degradation system of eukaryotic cells (Schmidt and Finley, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Proteasomes influence crucial processes in the cell including protein homeostasis, DNA repair, signal transduction and immune responses.
source: Proteasomes influence crucial processes in the cell including protein homeostasis, DNA repair, signal transduction and immune responses (Rousseau and Bertolotti, 2018) by degrading a multitude of regulatory, short-lived, damaged and misfolded proteins (Glickman and Ciechanover, 2002; Abildgaard et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Proteasomes degrade a multitude of regulatory, short-lived, damaged and misfolded proteins.
source: Proteasomes influence crucial processes in the cell including protein homeostasis, DNA repair, signal transduction and immune responses (Rousseau and Bertolotti, 2018) by degrading a multitude of regulatory, short-lived, damaged and misfolded proteins (Glickman and Ciechanover, 2002; Abildgaard et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Impairment of proteasome function has been described to occur during aging.
source: Impairment of proteasome function has been described to occur during aging Saez and Vilchez, 2014 and in neurodegenerative diseases Tanaka and Matsuda, 2014; Schmidt and Finley, 2014
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature.

claim: Impairment of proteasome function has been described in neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Impairment of proteasome function has been described to occur during aging Saez and Vilchez, 2014 and in neurodegenerative diseases Tanaka and Matsuda, 2014; Schmidt and Finley, 2014
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature.

claim: High expression levels of proteasome subunits have been linked to longevity in worms.
source: high expression levels of proteasome subunits have been linked to longevity in different species including worms (Vilchez et al., 2012), fish (Kelmer Sacramento et al., 2020), and flies (Tonoki et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: High expression levels of proteasome subunits have been linked to longevity in fish.
source: high expression levels of proteasome subunits have been linked to longevity in different species including worms (Vilchez et al., 2012), fish (Kelmer Sacramento et al., 2020), and flies (Tonoki et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: High expression levels of proteasome subunits have been linked to longevity in flies.
source: high expression levels of proteasome subunits have been linked to longevity in different species including worms (Vilchez et al., 2012), fish (Kelmer Sacramento et al., 2020), and flies (Tonoki et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: Partial proteasome inhibition is sufficient to induce cellular senescence.
source: While partial proteasome inhibition is sufficient to induce cellular senescence (Chondrogianni et al., 2003; Chondrogianni and Gonos, 2004), prolonged inhibition of the proteasome induces apoptosis (Abbas and Larisch, 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: Prolonged inhibition of the proteasome induces apoptosis.
source: While partial proteasome inhibition is sufficient to induce cellular senescence (Chondrogianni et al., 2003; Chondrogianni and Gonos, 2004), prolonged inhibition of the proteasome induces apoptosis (Abbas and Larisch, 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Cancer cells are especially sensitive to proteotoxic stress.
source: This has been exploited in cancer therapies, for example against blood cancers, as cancer cells are especially sensitive to proteotoxic stress (Manasanch and Orlowski, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: Peptide generation by specialized immunoproteasomes regulates antigen presentation.
source: In the immune system, peptide generation by specialized immunoproteasomes regulates antigen presentation and has been linked to auto-immune disorders (Feist et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: Immunoproteasomes have been linked to auto-immune disorders.
source: In the immune system, peptide generation by specialized immunoproteasomes regulates antigen presentation and has been linked to auto-immune disorders (Feist et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: The eukaryotic proteasome consists of two subcomplexes: the 'core particle' (20 S proteasome) and the 'regulatory particle' (19 S).
source: The eukaryotic proteasome consists of two subcomplexes: the 'core particle' (20 S proteasome) that can be present either alone or in association with one (26 S proteasome) or two 19 S 'regulatory particles' (30 S proteasome).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about proteasome structure.

claim: The 20S core particle can be present alone or in association with one or two 19S regulatory particles.
source: The eukaryotic proteasome consists of two subcomplexes: the 'core particle' (20 S proteasome) that can be present either alone or in association with one (26 S proteasome) or two 19 S 'regulatory particles' (30 S proteasome).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about proteasome assembly states.

claim: The core particle can be associated with alternative regulatory complexes including PA200 (PSME4).
source: In addition to the 19S regulatory particles, the core particle can be associated with different alternative regulatory complexes including the proteasome activator PA200 (named PSME4 in mammals) or three different versions of the 11S regulator complex PA28 – PA28α (PSME1), PA28β (PSME2), and PA28γ (PSME3).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about proteasome regulators.

claim: The core particle can be associated with three different versions of the 11S regulator complex PA28.
source: In addition to the 19S regulatory particles, the core particle can be associated with different alternative regulatory complexes including the proteasome activator PA200 (named PSME4 in mammals) or three different versions of the 11S regulator complex PA28 – PA28α (PSME1), PA28β (PSME2), and PA28γ (PSME3).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about proteasome regulators.

claim: PA28 regulators are ATP-independent proteasome regulators that modulate proteasome activity towards small peptides and unfolded proteins.
source: These are ATP-independent proteasome regulators that modulate proteasome activity towards small peptides and unfolded proteins and can facilitate protein degradation independent of ubiquitin (Toste Rêgo and da Fonseca, 2019; Mao et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature.

claim: PA28 regulators can facilitate protein degradation independent of ubiquitin.
source: These are ATP-independent proteasome regulators that modulate proteasome activity towards small peptides and unfolded proteins and can facilitate protein degradation independent of ubiquitin (Toste Rêgo and da Fonseca, 2019; Mao et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature.

claim: The composition of cellular proteasomes can be heterogeneous due to the assembly of distinct sub-complexes in variable stoichiometries.
source: The composition of cellular proteasomes can be heterogeneous due to the assembly of distinct sub-complexes in variable stoichiometries, and to the incorporation of tissue/cell type specific components.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about proteasome heterogeneity.

claim: Specialized proteasomes have been described in immune cells, thymus, sperm cells, and cancer.
source: Specialized proteasomes have been described in immune cells, thymus, sperm cells (Abi Habib et al., 2022), and cancer (Javitt et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature.

claim: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane.
source: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane (Albert et al., 2017), endoplasmic reticulum (Albert et al., 2020), Golgi apparatus (Eisenberg-Lerner et al., 2020), plasma membranes (Ramachandran and Margolis, 2017), primary cilia Gerhardt et al., 2016, and protein aggregates (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane (Albert et al., 2017), endoplasmic reticulum (Albert et al., 2020), Golgi apparatus (Eisenberg-Lerner et al., 2020), plasma membranes (Ramachandran and Margolis, 2017), primary cilia Gerhardt et al., 2016, and protein aggregates (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in the Golgi apparatus.
source: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane (Albert et al., 2017), endoplasmic reticulum (Albert et al., 2020), Golgi apparatus (Eisenberg-Lerner et al., 2020), plasma membranes (Ramachandran and Margolis, 2017), primary cilia Gerhardt et al., 2016, and protein aggregates (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located at plasma membranes.
source: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane (Albert et al., 2017), endoplasmic reticulum (Albert et al., 2020), Golgi apparatus (Eisenberg-Lerner et al., 2020), plasma membranes (Ramachandran and Margolis, 2017), primary cilia Gerhardt et al., 2016, and protein aggregates (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in primary cilia.
source: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane (Albert et al., 2017), endoplasmic reticulum (Albert et al., 2020), Golgi apparatus (Eisenberg-Lerner et al., 2020), plasma membranes (Ramachandran and Margolis, 2017), primary cilia Gerhardt et al., 2016, and protein aggregates (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in protein aggregates.
source: Sub-populations of proteasomes have been shown to be located in different cellular compartments including inner nuclear membrane (Albert et al., 2017), endoplasmic reticulum (Albert et al., 2020), Golgi apparatus (Eisenberg-Lerner et al., 2020), plasma membranes (Ramachandran and Margolis, 2017), primary cilia Gerhardt et al., 2016, and protein aggregates (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: The assembly state of proteasomes and their biophysical properties can be modulated in response to hyperosmotic stress.
source: Moreover, the assembly state of proteasomes and their biophysical properties can be modulated in response to, for example hyperosmotic stress (Yasuda et al., 2020) or amino acid starvation (Uriarte et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: The assembly state of proteasomes and their biophysical properties can be modulated in response to amino acid starvation.
source: Moreover, the assembly state of proteasomes and their biophysical properties can be modulated in response to, for example hyperosmotic stress (Yasuda et al., 2020) or amino acid starvation (Uriarte et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a specific study.

claim: Traditional methods such as co-immunoprecipitation, affinity purification or cell fractionation coupled to mass spectrometry have been valuable in studying proteasome interactions.
source: Traditional methods such as co-immunoprecipitation, affinity purification or cell fractionation coupled to mass spectrometry have been valuable in studying proteasome interactions (Fabre et al., 2013; Fabre et al., 2015; Bousquet-Dubouch et al., 2009; Geladaki et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2007), but they may not capture transient or weak interactions.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Traditional methods may not capture transient or weak proteasome interactions.
source: Traditional methods such as co-immunoprecipitation, affinity purification or cell fractionation coupled to mass spectrometry have been valuable in studying proteasome interactions (Fabre et al., 2013; Fabre et al., 2015; Bousquet-Dubouch et al., 2009; Geladaki et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2007), but they may not capture transient or weak interactions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of traditional methods.

claim: Proximity labeling assays such as BioID or APEX utilize engineered proteins that can biotinylate neighboring proteins in close proximity within the cellular context.
source: To address this limitation, proximity labeling assays, such as BioID or APEX, utilize engineered proteins that can biotinylate neighboring proteins in close proximity within the cellular context, and thereby enable a more comprehensive and dynamic characterization of protein-protein interactions (Gingras et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: Proximity labeling enables a more comprehensive and dynamic characterization of protein-protein interactions.
source: To address this limitation, proximity labeling assays, such as BioID or APEX, utilize engineered proteins that can biotinylate neighboring proteins in close proximity within the cellular context, and thereby enable a more comprehensive and dynamic characterization of protein-protein interactions (Gingras et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: The promiscuous biotin ligase BirA* was fused to the C-terminus of PSMA4/α3.
source: Based on previous studies where proteasome members were tagged with fluorescent proteins in mammalian cells (Salomons et al., 2010; Bingol and Schuman, 2006), we fused the promiscuous biotin ligase BirA* either to the C-termini of the 20 S core particle protein PSMA4/ɑ3, the 19 S particle base protein PSMC2/Rpt1 or the N-terminus of the 19 S particle lid protein PSMD3/Rpn3 (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design supported by figures.

claim: The promiscuous biotin ligase BirA* was fused to the C-terminus of PSMC2/Rpt1.
source: Based on previous studies where proteasome members were tagged with fluorescent proteins in mammalian cells (Salomons et al., 2010; Bingol and Schuman, 2006), we fused the promiscuous biotin ligase BirA* either to the C-termini of the 20 S core particle protein PSMA4/ɑ3, the 19 S particle base protein PSMC2/Rpt1 or the N-terminus of the 19 S particle lid protein PSMD3/Rpn3 (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design supported by figures.

claim: The promiscuous biotin ligase BirA* was fused to the N-terminus of PSMD3/Rpn3.
source: Based on previous studies where proteasome members were tagged with fluorescent proteins in mammalian cells (Salomons et al., 2010; Bingol and Schuman, 2006), we fused the promiscuous biotin ligase BirA* either to the C-termini of the 20 S core particle protein PSMA4/ɑ3, the 19 S particle base protein PSMC2/Rpt1 or the N-terminus of the 19 S particle lid protein PSMD3/Rpn3 (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design supported by figures.

claim: Each BirA* fusion construct contained a FLAG tag for fusion protein detection.
source: Each construct also contained a FLAG tag for fusion protein detection.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Stable HEK293 FlpIn TREx cell lines were generated that overexpress the BirA* fusion proteins under the control of a tetracycline inducible promoter.
source: We used these constructs to generate stable HEK293 FlpIn TREx (HEK293T) cell lines that overexpress the BirA* fusion proteins under the control of a tetracycline inducible promoter.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Tetracycline-dependent expression of BirA* fusion proteins was confirmed by anti-FLAG immunoblot.
source: We confirmed tetracycline-dependent expression of the corresponding cell lines by anti-FLAG immunoblot, and confirmed biotinylating activity following supplementation of exogenous biotin using streptavidin-HRP blot (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Biotinylating activity of BirA* fusion proteins was confirmed following supplementation of exogenous biotin using streptavidin-HRP blot.
source: We confirmed tetracycline-dependent expression of the corresponding cell lines by anti-FLAG immunoblot, and confirmed biotinylating activity following supplementation of exogenous biotin using streptavidin-HRP blot (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Expression and biotinylation results were validated by immunofluorescence analysis.
source: These results were validated by immunofluorescence analysis (Figure 1c and Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in figures.

claim: The optimized BioID protocol reduced streptavidin contamination more than fourfold.
source: These optimizations allowed us to drastically reduce (>fourfold) the background from streptavidin-derived peptides (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b and c), and to increase more than twofold the number of identified proteins and biotinylated peptides in our BioID experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The optimized BioID protocol increased more than twofold the number of identified proteins and biotinylated peptides.
source: These optimizations allowed us to drastically reduce (>fourfold) the background from streptavidin-derived peptides (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b and c), and to increase more than twofold the number of identified proteins and biotinylated peptides in our BioID experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Significant enrichment of proteasome subunits was found for each of the cell lines expressing BirA* fusion proteins compared to BirA* control.
source: We found significant enrichment of proteasome subunits for each of the cell lines expressing BirA* fusion proteins compared to BirA* control (Figure 1—figure supplement 2f and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The pattern of enrichment varied between fusion proteins.
source: However, the pattern of enrichment varied between fusion proteins (Figure 1d and e).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in figures.

claim: PSMA4-BirA* provided the strongest enrichment for 20 S proteins.
source: PSMA4-BirA* provided the strongest enrichment for 20 S proteins, but also a prominent enrichment of other proteasome components (typically >4 fold), while PSMC2-BirA* enriched preferentially 19 S base proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: PSMA4-BirA* provided prominent enrichment of other proteasome components (typically >4 fold).
source: PSMA4-BirA* provided the strongest enrichment for 20 S proteins, but also a prominent enrichment of other proteasome components (typically >4 fold), while PSMC2-BirA* enriched preferentially 19 S base proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: PSMC2-BirA* enriched preferentially 19 S base proteins.
source: PSMA4-BirA* provided the strongest enrichment for 20 S proteins, but also a prominent enrichment of other proteasome components (typically >4 fold), while PSMC2-BirA* enriched preferentially 19 S base proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: BirA*-PSMD3 displayed a more homogenous, but less pronounced enrichment of proteasome proteins (typically ~twofold).
source: BirA*-PSMD3 displayed a more homogenous, but less pronounced enrichment of proteasome proteins (typically ~twofold).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: The abundance levels of PSMA4-BirA* are comparable to the ones of the endogenous PSMA4.
source: Since the BirA* fusion protein is over-expressed using a CMV promoter, we first confirmed that the abundance levels of PSMA4-BirA* are comparable to the ones of the endogenous PSMA4 using an anti-PSMA4 immunoblot (Figure 2a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunoblot data shown in figures.

claim: Size exclusion chromatography coupled to quantitative mass spectrometry revealed three major distinct peaks corresponding to the major assembly states of the proteasome.
source: Protein elution profiles built from mass spectrometry data obtained from 32 SEC fractions revealed three major distinct peaks corresponding to the major assembly states of the proteasome (Supplementary file 2). These include 30 S proteasomes, containing a core particle capped with two regulatory particles, 26 S proteasomes, containing a core particle capped with 1 regulatory particle, and isolated core particles (20 S proteasomes; Figure 2b and Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by SEC-MS data shown in figures.

claim: The majority of the BirA* signal (~60%) correlated with the elution profile of other proteasome components in all the assembly states.
source: With the exception of a peak in lower molecular weight fractions (~fraction 20), likely representing intermediate complex assemblies, the majority of the BirA* signal (~60%) correlated with the elution profile of other proteasome components in all the assembly states (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by SEC-MS data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Anti-FLAG immunoblot upon blue native gel electrophoresis confirmed the incorporation of PSMA4-BirA* into assembled proteasomes.
source: We have additionally performed anti-FLAG immunoblot upon blue native gel electrophoresis (BN-PAGE) to confirm the incorporation of PSMA4-BirA* into assembled proteasomes, and to demonstrate that the assembly of proteasomes is not affected by the overexpression of PSMA4-BirA* (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The assembly of proteasomes is not affected by the overexpression of PSMA4-BirA*.
source: We have additionally performed anti-FLAG immunoblot upon blue native gel electrophoresis (BN-PAGE) to confirm the incorporation of PSMA4-BirA* into assembled proteasomes, and to demonstrate that the assembly of proteasomes is not affected by the overexpression of PSMA4-BirA* (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: 25 out of 26 residues identified as biotinylated by PSMA4-BirA* are located less than 10 nm away from the C-terminus of PSMA4.
source: By mapping the identified sites on the proteasome structure, we could confirm the specificity of protein biotinylation by showing that 25 out of 26 residues identified as biotinylated by PSMA4-BirA* are located less than 10 nm away from the C-terminus of PSMA4 (Figure 2d and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data and structural analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: 18 of the biotinylated sites were located on proteins from the 19 S regulatory particle.
source: Importantly, 18 of these sites were located on proteins from the 19 S regulatory particle, further supporting the incorporation of PSMA4-BirA* into assembled proteasomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data and structural analysis.

claim: A slight, not-significant reduction of proteasome activity (~15–20%) was observed following addition of tetracycline.
source: We observed a slight, not-significant reduction of proteasome activity (~15–20%) following addition of tetracycline that was comparable between cell lines expressing proteasome PSMA4-BirA* or BirA* control (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by proteasome activity assay data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Tetracycline-mediated induction of PSMA4-BirA* did not have a major effect on the degradation kinetics of c-Myc.
source: We showed that tetracycline-mediated induction of PSMA4-BirA* did not have a major effect on the degradation kinetics of c-Myc (Figure 2f and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cycloheximide chase experiment data shown in figures.

claim: Levels of K48-ubiquitylated proteins were not affected by PSMA4-BirA* overexpression.
source: Also, levels of K48-ubiquitylated proteins were not affected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d), further confirming that PSMA4-BirA* has no major impact on the proteolytic activity of the proteasome in cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunoblot data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: 608 protein groups were identified as enriched by ProteasomeID for the PSMA4-BirA* dataset (false positive rate, FPR <0.05).
source: Using the classifier, we identified 608 protein groups enriched by ProteasomeID for the PSMA4-BirA* dataset (false positive rate, FPR <0.05, Figure 3c and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data and classifier analysis shown in Figure 3c.

claim: SEC elution profiles of proteins enriched in ProteasomeID tend to have significantly higher correlation with the elution profile of PSMA4.
source: We could show that SEC elution profiles of proteins enriched in ProteasomeID tend to have significantly higher correlation with the elution profile of PSMA4 (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by SEC-MS data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: 72 proteins overlapping between ProteasomeID and previous proteomic studies include almost all known proteasome members, assembly factors, and activators.
source: We found 72 proteins overlapping to our dataset including almost all known proteasome members, assembly factors, and activators (Figure 3e and f).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by comparison with previous studies shown in Figure 3e and f.

claim: 304 out of 608 (50%) ProteasomeID enriched proteins could be matched to known proteasome-interacting proteins or their direct binding partners.
source: Therefore, in total, 304 out of 608 (50%) ProteasomeID enriched proteins could be matched to known proteasome-interacting proteins or their direct binding partners.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by network analysis and comparison with databases.

claim: 2 hours were sufficient for miniTurbo to achieve biotinylation levels comparable to PSMA4-BirA* after 24 hours of biotin supplementation.
source: We tested biotinylation by PSMA4-miniTurbo using immunoblot and confirmed that 2 hr were sufficient to achieve biotinylation levels comparable to the one PSMA4-BirA* after 24 hr of biotin supplementation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunoblot data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: 168 protein groups were identified as enriched for PSMA4-miniTurbo (FPR <0.05).
source: Applying the classifier algorithm, we identified 168 protein groups enriched for PSMA4-miniTurbo (FPR <0.05, Figure 4—figure supplement 1f and g).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data and classifier analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: A subset of 141 proteins were enriched exclusively upon MG132 treatment.
source: Comparison of ProteasomeID enriched proteins from cells treated with proteasome inhibitor versus vehicle control revealed a subset of 141 proteins enriched exclusively upon MG132 treatment (Figure 4b and c).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and c.

claim: 77 out of 133 proteins (58%) enriched upon MG132 treatment have been shown to display increased ubiquitylation upon proteasome inhibition.
source: Of the remaining 133 proteins, 77 (58%) have been shown in a previous study Trulsson et al., 2022 to display increased ubiquitylation (as assessed by GlyGly enrichment and MS analysis) upon proteasome inhibition, and 39 are reported proteasome substrates such as MYC, ATF4, and PINK1 (Figure 4c and d and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by comparison with a previous study and mass spectrometry data.

claim: 39 proteins enriched upon MG132 treatment are reported proteasome substrates such as MYC, ATF4, and PINK1.
source: Of the remaining 133 proteins, 77 (58%) have been shown in a previous study Trulsson et al., 2022 to display increased ubiquitylation (as assessed by GlyGly enrichment and MS analysis) upon proteasome inhibition, and 39 are reported proteasome substrates such as MYC, ATF4, and PINK1 (Figure 4c and d and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data and literature.

claim: ARMC6, BRAT1, and TIGD5 were validated as proteasome substrates by cycloheximide chase experiment.
source: We then performed a cycloheximide chase experiment and could validate them as proteasome substrates (Figure 4g and Figure 4—figure supplement 1j).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cycloheximide chase experiment data shown in figures.

claim: Prominent enrichment of BRD containing proteins was detected following treatment with KB02-JQ1.
source: Importantly, we could detect prominent enrichment of BRD containing proteins following treatment with KB02-JQ1 (Figure 5b and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The enrichment effect of KB02-JQ1 was more pronounced for BRD2 and BRD3 and less striking for BRD4.
source: The effect was more pronounced for BRD2 and BRD3 and less striking for BRD4 (Figure 5c), presumably reflecting different kinetics of induced degradation by KB02-JQ1 (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The enrichment of BRD2 and BRD3 was detectable in absence of MG132, in contrast to endogenous substrates.
source: Notably, the enrichment of BRD2 and BRD3 was also detectable in absence of MG132, in contrast to endogenous substrates that become enriched only following proteasome inhibition (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: A mouse line was generated enabling doxycycline inducible expression of the PSMA4-miniTurbo construct in all tissues.
source: The obtained mouse line constitutively expresses the rtTA3 transactivator, thereby enabling doxycycline inducible expression of the PSMA4-miniTurbo construct in all tissues.
evidence: This is a description of the mouse model generated in the study.

claim: No significant changes in body weight nor any sign of suffering were observed in mice fed with doxycycline containing food.
source: We observed no significant changes in body weight nor any sign of suffering (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Immunoblot analysis confirmed expression of PSMA4-miniTurbo in all organs except the brain.
source: Immunoblot analysis confirmed expression of PSMA4-miniTurbo in all organs except the brain (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunoblot data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The limited penetration of food-administered doxycycline limits the usability of the approach in the brain.
source: The locus used for PSMA4-miniTurbo expression (Col1a1) is known to be active in all the organs tested (Lee, 2014), however the limited penetration of food-administered doxycycline (Gengenbacher et al., 2020) limits the usability of our approach in the brain.
evidence: This is an inference based on known limitations of doxycycline delivery and supported by citations.
